github.copilot.chat.commitMessageGenerat.text: Generate a single concise commit message for this DSA practice repository based only on the staged changes.
Analyze the staged file names, folder names, source code, comments, and git diff before generating the commit message.
Use lowercase commit types followed by a colon and one space.
Use one of these commit types: solve, add, fix, optimize, refactor, docs.
Use 'solve' when a new DSA problem, coding problem, or algorithm solution is added.
Use 'add' when adding a new alternative approach or implementation to an already solved problem.
Use 'fix' when correcting wrong logic, edge cases, overflow, indexing, conditions, or other bugs in an existing solution.
Use 'optimize' when the primary change improves time complexity, space complexity, or algorithmic efficiency.
Use 'refactor' when restructuring or cleaning existing code without changing the algorithm or expected behavior.
Use 'docs' when the staged changes only update comments, explanations, notes, or documentation.
For a newly solved LeetCode problem, use exactly: solve: <4-digit problem number> <official LeetCode problem title>
Always pad LeetCode problem numbers to exactly 4 digits. Example: 1 becomes 0001, 9 becomes 0009, 350 becomes 0350, and 509 becomes 0509.
For LeetCode problems, use the official problem title with correct capitalization when the problem identity is clearly available from the staged file name, code, or comments.
Never guess or invent a LeetCode problem number. If the LeetCode identity cannot be determined confidently from the staged changes, treat it as a normal DSA problem.
For a newly solved non-LeetCode DSA problem or algorithm, use: solve: <Problem or Algorithm Name>
For non-LeetCode problems, infer a clean human-readable title from the file name, folder name, function name, class name, comments, and implementation.
Convert camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and file names into a clean title. Example: selectionSort.cpp becomes Selection Sort and recursive_bubble_sort.cpp becomes Recursive Bubble Sort.
Do not include file extensions, folder names, implementation details, or programming language names unless they are essential to identify the problem.
For an alternative solution to an existing problem, use: add: <Problem Name> alternative approach
For a bug fix, use: fix: <Problem Name> <short description of the corrected issue>
For an algorithmic optimization, use: optimize: <Problem Name> <short description of the optimization>
For code restructuring, use: refactor: <Problem Name>
For documentation-only changes, use: docs: <Topic or Problem Name>
If multiple staged files belong to the same problem or algorithm, generate one commit message describing that problem.
If multiple staged files represent unrelated problems, generate one concise commit message summarizing the common DSA topic. Do not list every file or create multiple commit messages.
Prefer the actual problem or algorithm name over generic descriptions such as add solution, update code, modify files, implement function, or code changes.
Keep the commit message short, specific, and written in imperative repository style.
Do not end the commit message with a period.
Do not use emojis.
Do not add a commit body, description, bullet points, markdown, scope, or extra explanation.
Output exactly one line containing only the commit message.
Examples: solve: 0350 Intersection of Two Arrays II
Examples: solve: 0509 Fibonacci Number
Examples: solve: Selection Sort
Examples: solve: Recursive Bubble Sort
Examples: add: Intersection of Two Arrays II alternative approach
Examples: fix: Reverse Integer overflow handling
Examples: optimize: Prime Check reduce iteration to square root
Examples: refactor: Selection Sort
Examples: docs: Hashing
